decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit extends the firm's core airfield lighting line, so it costs little to carry, and airport capital spending held back by COVID means its value is still unresolved.
The air situation display complements the surveillance portfolio, including the MLAT flagship, and nothing shows it has failed, so the cheap option is worth holding while air traffic recovers.
The systems training program builds on existing know-how and staff, costs very little to keep, and supports customer lock-in as airports restaff after the pandemic.
The airfield ground lighting course is a low-cost add-on to the core lighting business, and its prospects remain open rather than shown to be poor.
The collaboration software fits the firm's stated move toward integrated, data-driven operations, and demand for it is uncertain but potentially large, which favors keeping the option alive.
The multilateration system is the flagship of the firm's surveillance direction and the uncertainty about its value has not resolved, so management will keep investing in it.
